claims_about_writeup.why: contribution.md does contain the full method write-up (mind-occupancy steering, its derivation from the white-bear contrast, and the ground-rules compliance), so the pointer is accurate.

differences.message_quote: the occupancy direction has cosine ≈ 0.88 with the think/don't-think direction (so it isolates the same operative signal, but via a single-sided construction with no "don't think" half), and both plateau at the same 0.78 ceiling on this split.
differences.what: The message discloses a quantitative overlap measure (cosine ≈0.88) and matching performance ceiling with the white-bear (WBS) think/don't-think direction, admitting the two vectors largely isolate the same signal. The write-up only argues qualitatively that the construction 'isolates a cleaner ingredient' and never reports this similarity/ceiling, so it presents the method as more clearly distinct from WBS.

message_source_quote: The intervention is a **mind-occupancy** direction, built from a contrast the white-bear paper doesn't use
writeup_source_quote: White-bear steering (Raman et al. 2026, `papers/`) showed a stance vector at layers 20–24 can stop that drop, but its vector contrasts "think about X" vs "do not think about X"
rationale: Both documents name and credit Raman et al. 2026 / white-bear steering (WBS) as the prior work whose layer band and stance-vector idea this method builds on, and both frame the novelty as replacing WBS's think/don't-think contrast with a presence-vs-absence-of-a-held-concept contrast. The message goes further than the write-up by quantifying how close the result actually is to WBS (cosine ≈0.88, same 0.78 ceiling), an admission of overlap that is absent from the write-up's purely qualitative novelty argument.
